To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
leadership transitions in a college or university can have a negative impact on the institution’s capital campaign.

(1) leadership transitions during fundraising campaigns are disruptive, but not fatal; (2) leadership transitions are disruptive because of the negative impact on morale, timing, momentum, and public relations; (3) leadership transitions during capital campaigns are disruptive, and they can be mitigated by training and development of interim and full-time provosts and vice-presidents.

(1) leadership transitions during fundraising campaigns have a negative impact on morale, timing, and momentum; (2) transitions during fundraising campaigns are disruptive, but do not prevent the campaigns from reaching their financial goals; and (3) provosts are often unprepared to assume leadership of a capital campaign.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of transitions in leadership during capital campaigns.
how leadership transitions affect fundraising campaigns.
how the leadership transitions during capital campaigns affect the campaigns themselves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
leadership transition is disruptive to a campaign, and the degree to which it disrupts the campaign is related to the degree to which the leadership transition is disruptive.
capital campaigns can and do continue to succeed despite changes in leadership, although the process is more difficult and time-consuming than if the president remains in place.
the leadership transitions during fundraising campaigns are a challenge to be addressed by institutions of higher education.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
leadership transitions can be disruptive, but they do not have to be.
the impact of leadership transitions on the success of capital campaigns depends on the timing of the transition and the quality of the leadership team.
leadership transitions during fundraising campaigns have a negative impact on the institution and the campaign.
The main takeaway from our work is that
leadership transitions during capital campaigns are inevitable and disruptive, yet the institution can still meet its financial goals if it is prepared for the transition.
leadership transitions are inevitable, but can be managed to minimize negative impact on fundraising campaigns.
capital campaigns can survive transitions, but only with a strong, committed, and well-trained fundraising leadership.
